title: When and how people first reached the Americas
summary: The precise date of the peopling of the Americas is a long-standing open question. Evidence for pre-Clovis people has accumulated, but key early dates remain contested.
why: It is the last continental-scale human arrival, and its timing shapes everything after it.
question: When did people first enter the Americas, and by which route?
evidence: White Sands footprints dated 21,000–23,000 years ago are contested; Monte Verde dates still debated; the ice-free corridor may have opened later than the earliest accepted sites.
wouldSettle: Undisputed, securely dated human remains or tools older than about 16,000 years, plus route-specific sites.

theories.name: Pacific coastal route
theories.idea: People travelled along the coast of the Pacific while inland ice still blocked the interior.

theories.name: Ice-free interior corridor
theories.idea: People walked south through a gap between ice sheets, though it may have opened too late.

theories.name: Clovis first
theories.idea: The older view that Clovis was the earliest culture, now challenged by pre-Clovis evidence.
